investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-07-04T07:15–07:22Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the production cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the remote agent pod because 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the agent VM was never provisioned, and the eval runner received no evidence — leaving all four required contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) missing.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes in the production-api cluster. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity (0 allocatable slots remaining), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable. As a result, the pod remained Unschedulable for 132–145 seconds across all three checks, the agent VM was never created, and the eval runner produced an empty evidence object — violating every assertion in the remote-agent-create expected-output contract.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: all allocatable peer-pod VM slots are consumed by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote agent pods.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 non-kata nodes do not match the pod's required node selector/affinity, meaning only 2 nodes are ever eligible, and those 2 are at capacity.
Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning: the production cluster has only 2 kata-capable nodes total, which may be insufficient for concurrent remote agent eval runs plus live workloads.

Lower probability — a recent node or resource quota change reduced available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots without a corresponding scale-out of kata-capable nodes (no suspect changes are present in sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges to support this hypothesis directly).

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing — Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Blocking Pod Scheduling
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the required kata peer-pod VM onto any of the 6 available nodes — 2 nodes reported insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. The eval probe never reached the agent creation step, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was collected and the expected-output contract was entirely unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the 2 nodes that support that resource class. The remaining 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. With zero viable scheduling targets and no preemption victims available, every remote-agent pod submitted during this eval window was stuck Unschedulable for 130–150 seconds before the eval timed out. Because the agent pod never started, the runner in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs (line 1905: createAgent) could not return an agent identity, and the state-polling step that depends on it never executed, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) absent. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agents Kubernetes node pool; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: the extended resource quota for peer-pod VMs is fully consumed, leaving no capacity for new eval pods. All three sibling checks report the same scheduler message, confirming this is a shared infrastructure constraint rather than an eval-specific bug.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's affinity rules, reducing the schedulable pool to only 2 nodes. If affinity rules were recently tightened or node labels changed, the effective capacity could have dropped suddenly.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning for the remote-agents node pool: the total number of kata-capable nodes (2) may be insufficient to absorb concurrent eval runs plus any live workloads, causing resource contention.
Lower probability — transient spike in live remote-agent workloads consuming all kata.peerpods.io/vm slots at the time of the eval run, which would be self-resolving once those workloads complete.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-07-04T07:15–07:22Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the production cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the remote agent pod because 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the agent VM was never provisioned, and the eval runner received no evidence — leaving all four required contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) missing.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes in the production-api cluster. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity (0 allocatable slots remaining), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable. As a result, the pod remained Unschedulable for 132–145 seconds across all three checks, the agent VM was never created, and the eval runner produced an empty evidence object — violating every assertion in the remote-agent-create expected-output contract.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: all allocatable peer-pod VM slots are consumed by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote agent pods.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 non-kata nodes do not match the pod's required node selector/affinity, meaning only 2 nodes are ever eligible, and those 2 are at capacity.
Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning: the production cluster has only 2 kata-capable nodes total, which may be insufficient for concurrent remote agent eval runs plus live workloads.

Lower probability — a recent node or resource quota change reduced available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots without a corresponding scale-out of kata-capable nodes (no suspect changes are present in sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges to support this hypothesis directly).

investigations.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing — Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Blocking Pod Scheduling
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the required kata peer-pod VM onto any of the 6 available nodes — 2 nodes reported insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. The eval probe never reached the agent creation step, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was collected and the expected-output contract was entirely unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the 2 nodes that support that resource class. The remaining 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. With zero viable scheduling targets and no preemption victims available, every remote-agent pod submitted during this eval window was stuck Unschedulable for 130–150 seconds before the eval timed out. Because the agent pod never started, the runner in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs (line 1905: createAgent) could not return an agent identity, and the state-polling step that depends on it never executed, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) absent. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agents Kubernetes node pool; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe node on the 2 kata-capable nodes shows available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots greater than zero at the time of the eval run, resource exhaustion is not the cause and a different scheduler rejection reason should be investigated.

If the remote-agent-create sibling check passes in a subsequent run while remote-agent-state still fails, the failure is not a shared pod scheduling problem but is specific to the state-polling logic in the runner.

If the pod affinity/selector rules were recently changed to intentionally exclude the 4 non-matching nodes and the 2 remaining nodes have capacity, the failure would be a configuration regression rather than resource exhaustion.

If a re-run of the eval immediately after the observed failure window succeeds and produces all four required evidence fields, the failure was a transient capacity spike rather than a sustained resource exhaustion condition.

If the Kubernetes event log for the eval namespace shows the pod eventually scheduled and running (but the eval timed out before it became ready), the root cause would be slow VM provisioning latency rather than hard resource exhaustion.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check that queries the Kubernetes API for kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested capacity on all kata-capable nodes and fails with a WARN before pod creation is attempted, providing earlier signal on resource exhaustion.

Add a node-pool health eval that verifies the expected number of nodes matching the remote-agent nodeAffinity/selector are in Ready state, catching label drift or node loss before it causes scheduling failures.

Add a pod-scheduling latency eval that measures time-to-scheduled for a remote-agent pod and warns if it exceeds a threshold (e.g., 30s), distinguishing slow provisioning from hard Unschedulable failures.

Extend the remote-agent-create eval to capture and surface the Kubernetes scheduler reason (Unschedulable, resource type, node count) as structured evidence fields, making future failures easier to triage without inspecting raw messages.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 3 Remote-Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment with identical Kubernetes scheduling errors: the 6-node cluster has only 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource, both of which are at capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no pod could be scheduled, the agent VM was never provisioned, and the eval runner never received any response evidence — leaving all 5 required contract fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) absent.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing remote agent provisioning in production-api has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 eligible nodes. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state) confirms that no schedulable capacity exists for peer-pod VMs at the time of the eval run. The eval runner calls createAgent with type "remote" (run-status-probes.mjs line 1918), which triggers VM provisioning; when the pod cannot be scheduled within the eval timeout window (~143s), the probe fails before any agent response can be captured, producing zero evidence and a complete contract gap.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:262-270: contract requires orgId, agentId, model, provider, message and asserts message containsIgnoreCase 'hello from aura' — none reachable without a running VM
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: concurrent workloads or prior eval runs consumed all available peer-pod VM slots, leaving zero capacity for new scheduling requests at the time of the eval run.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes carry, permanently restricting the schedulable pool to those 2 nodes and making the cluster more susceptible to capacity exhaustion.

Tertiary — insufficient cluster capacity for the remote-agent workload class: the cluster may be undersized (only 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes) relative to the concurrent demand from eval probes plus production traffic, with no preemption policy configured ('No preemption victims found', 'Preemption is not helpful for scheduling' per failed-check.message).

Lower probability — a transient spike in remote agent creation requests (e.g., from other eval runs or user traffic) temporarily exhausted VM slots that would otherwise be available; this would be self-resolving and would not explain all three sibling checks failing sequentially across a ~5-minute window.

recommendedNextActions: Investigate current kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the 2 eligible production nodes immediately — determine whether slots are held by stuck or leaked pods from prior eval runs or user workloads, and release them if so.

Check whether any remote-agent pods from the failing eval run (started around 2026-07-04T07:17-07:22Z) are still in Pending or Terminating state and consuming VM quota; force-delete them if cleanup did not complete.

Assess whether the 2-node kata.peerpods.io/vm pool is sized appropriately for concurrent eval probe runs plus production remote-agent demand; if not, plan capacity expansion or add more nodes with the required label/taint.

Investigate why 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector — determine if this is intentional topology isolation or an unintended configuration that unnecessarily restricts the schedulable pool.
Review whether the eval runner's withCleanup mechanism (run-status-probes.mjs) reliably releases VM resources after each probe run to prevent slot leakage across successive eval executions.

Consider adding a pre-flight capacity check to the remote-agent eval probes that verifies kata.peerpods.io/vm availability before attempting agent creation, to produce a more actionable SKIP or WARN status instead of a timeout-driven FAIL.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe node output shows kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity is available and not exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes, the scheduling failure has a different cause (e.g., a misconfigured resource request in the pod spec).

If the 4 non-matching nodes are shown to have kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity but are excluded only by a recently changed node affinity rule, the root cause shifts to a node selector/affinity misconfiguration rather than capacity exhaustion.
If a re-run of the eval immediately after this failure succeeds and produces all 5 required evidence fields, the failure was a transient capacity spike rather than a sustained exhaustion condition.

If no other pods or workloads are found consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on the 2 eligible nodes at the time of failure, the root cause may be a resource quota or limit range restriction rather than actual VM slot exhaustion.

If the local-agent-runtime sibling check (which shares the same evidence contract shape per check-expectations.json lines 102-105) also fails with a scheduling error, the problem may be broader than the remote-agent VM pool.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check that queries the Kubernetes API for kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested counts on all eligible nodes and warns when available capacity falls below a minimum threshold (e.g., 1 free slot).
Add a pre-flight node affinity/selector validation eval that confirms the expected number of nodes match the remote-agent pod selector before attempting VM provisioning.
Add a pod cleanup health eval that detects Pending or Terminating remote-agent pods older than a configurable TTL, to catch VM slot leakage from prior eval runs.

Extend the remote-agent-create eval to emit a structured scheduling-failure evidence key when the pod enters Unschedulable state, enabling the contract validator to distinguish a scheduling failure from a runtime failure.
